section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department, Department of the Army, and inter-agency (SWNCC/SANACC) records from September to December 1947 concerning economic recovery, reparations, and reform in occupied Japan. Key topics include inter-departmental conflicts over SWNCC/SANACC 380, 381, and 384 regarding whether to foster Japanese economic recovery through unilateral U.S. directives or multilateral action via the Far Eastern Commission. The materials also assess business criticisms of occupation economic programs, prominently James L. Kauffman's report attacking zaibatsu deconcentration and labor rights, as well as inquiries regarding trade credits, gold reserves, and research on Japan's economy.

subfiles.about: Argues that deconcentration of economic power and dissolving zaibatsu monopolies will foster representative government and pro-American alignment in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Page eight of an analysis asserting that deconcentrating economic power promotes parliamentary democracy and prevents quasi-socialist business monopolies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Economic Deconcentration and Democratization in Japan (Fragment)

subfiles.about: Records discussions regarding authority to pledge Japanese convertible gold reserves for cotton credits and revising SCAP Circular No. 9.
subfiles.from: Participants (Cleveland, Baldwin, Snow, Whitman, McDiarmid, Evans)
subfiles.summary: State, War, and Export-Import Bank officials review legal authority under Far Eastern Commission policy to pledge Japanese gold reserves as collateral for trade credits.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Use of Gold Fund and SCAP Circular No. 9

subfiles.about: Harvard University filing sheet recording Professor Seymour E. Harris's inquiry concerning the Japanese Economic White Paper.
subfiles.summary: Filing cover sheet for correspondence from Professor Seymour E. Harris regarding the Japanese Economic White Paper.
subfiles.title: Cover Sheet for Inquiry from Professor Seymour E. Harris

subfiles.about: Transmits two copies of the Japanese Economic White Paper to Professor Seymour E. Harris.
subfiles.summary: Edwin M. Martin forwards copies of the Japanese Economic White Paper and clarifies quotation rights for Tokyo press excerpts.
subfiles.title: Letter from Edwin M. Martin to Professor Seymour E. Harris

subfiles.about: Transmits a British Commonwealth Conference paper on post-treaty economic policy for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Barnett forwards a Canberra conference paper reflecting British Commonwealth perspectives on post-treaty Japanese economic and security controls.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Robert W. Barnett to Edwin M. Martin Regarding Canberra Document

subfiles.about: Sets forth British Commonwealth recommendations on post-treaty industrial security controls, democratization, reparations, and property restoration in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Proposes selective controls on heavy industries, support for land reform and zaibatsu dissolution, realistic reparations limits, and restitution of Allied property.
subfiles.title: British Commonwealth Conference, Canberra: Supplementary Notes on Economic and Financial Problems

subfiles.about: Details State Department objections to Army proposals in SWNCC 384 for unilateral directives on Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: State Member Saltzman opposes issuing unilateral directives that bypass the Far Eastern Commission or relax agreed level-of-industry standards, warning of Allied resentment.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Charles E. Saltzman on SWNCC 384: The Economic Recovery of Japan

subfiles.about: Records receipt of a Western Union telegram from Eugene P. Thomas regarding Japanese economic directives.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip conveying a telegram from National Foreign Trade Council President Eugene P. Thomas to Under Secretary Clayton.
subfiles.title: Department of State Routing Slip for Telegram from Eugene P. Thomas

subfiles.about: Explains the confidential status of Far Eastern Commission policy proposals on excessive concentration of economic power (FEC-230).
subfiles.summary: Whitman explains that FEC-230 remains confidential pending international negotiation, but encloses published FEC policy decisions on Japanese economic matters.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Eugene P. Thomas Regarding FEC-230

subfiles.about: Transmits a State Department redraft of SWNCC 380 regarding procedures for unilateral directives on Japanese economic problems.
subfiles.summary: State Member submits a substitute paper for SWNCC 380 establishing formal written polling before issuing unilateral directives.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum by Charles E. Saltzman on SWNCC 380 and 380/1 (Unilateral Action)

subfiles.about: Submits a State Department redraft of SWNCC 380 and 380/1 regarding unilateral action on Japanese economic matters.
subfiles.summary: Formal transmittal to SANACC of a redraft establishing formal polling procedures for issuing unilateral interim directives on economic matters.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Charles E. Saltzman on SWNCC 380 and 380/1 (Unilateral Action)

subfiles.about: Outlines U.S. policy and procedures for establishing deadlines and issuing unilateral interim directives on urgent Japanese economic issues.
subfiles.summary: Reviews FEC authority and proposes setting deadlines for Commission decisions on urgent economic problems, after which the U.S. may issue interim directives if SANACC concurs.
subfiles.title: Draft Statement by State Member SANACC: Unilateral Action on Japanese Economic Problems

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum by attorney James Lee Kauffman criticizing occupation economic policies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Francis White forwards James Lee Kauffman's memorandum detailing critical impressions of economic conditions and reforms in occupied Japan.
subfiles.title: Letter from Francis White to W. Walton Butterworth, Jr. Regarding Kauffman Memorandum

subfiles.about: Forwards approved copies of SANACC 380/2 on unilateral action on Japanese economic problems to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of approved paper SANACC 380/2 for Department information and for the guidance of the U.S. Member of the FEC.
subfiles.title: SANACC Memorandum SANA-5783 for the Secretary of State (SANACC 380/2)

subfiles.about: Records instructions from SANACC Secretary Moseley to act upon SANA-5783.
subfiles.summary: File note noting SANACC Secretary Moseley's instruction to take action based on the attached copy of SANA-5783.
subfiles.title: File Note Regarding SANA-5783

subfiles.about: Corrected copy transmitting SANACC 380/2 regarding unilateral action on Japanese economic problems with agency distribution.
subfiles.summary: Corrected copy of memorandum forwarding SANACC 380/2 on unilateral economic directives, showing official committee distribution.
subfiles.title: Corrected Copy of SANACC Memorandum SANA-5783 for the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Transmits SANACC 380/2 regarding unilateral action on economic problems to the U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Wisner forwards SANACC 380/2 to General McCoy for his guidance regarding unilateral U.S. policy actions on Japanese economic matters.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Frank G. Wisner to the U.S. Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Analyzes legal and policy ramifications of proposed Army revisions to SANACC 381/1 regarding the Japanese economy.
subfiles.summary: Whitman examines legal questions regarding Army proposals to unilaterally rescind provisions of earlier occupation directives disclaiming economic responsibility.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Roswell H. Whitman to P. P. Claxton Regarding Army Revision of SANACC 381/1

subfiles.about: Draft memorandum detailing procedural mechanisms for polling members on unilateral economic directives under SWNCC 380.
subfiles.summary: Draft memorandum explaining proposed secretarial polling procedures before issuing unilateral directives on Japanese economic matters.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum by Charles E. Saltzman on SWNCC 380 and 380/1 (Variant Text)

subfiles.about: Transmits an OE analysis evaluating James L. Kauffman's critical report on economic reforms in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Whitman transmits an internal OE memorandum evaluating and rebutting James L. Kauffman's report on Japanese economic reform programs.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Roswell H. Whitman to Jacques J. Reinstein Transmitting Kauffman Report Analysis

subfiles.about: Provides a thorough State Department rebuttal of James L. Kauffman's report criticizing SCAP economic reforms in Japan.
subfiles.from: Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs
subfiles.summary: This extensive State Department memorandum refutes James L. Kauffman's criticisms of SCAP's deconcentration, land reform, and trade union policies. It defends these reforms as essential to dismantle the authoritarian zaibatsu-government alliance, foster a democratic middle class, and insulate Japan from communist appeal. It maintains that economic stagnation is caused by wartime destruction and shortages of imported raw materials rather than occupation reforms, warning that restoring the pre-war oligarchy would discredit American policy.
subfiles.title: Analysis of Mr. J. L. Kauffman's Report on Conditions in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a proposed statement for General McCoy to deliver before the Far Eastern Commission regarding Japanese recovery.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman agrees with Draper on prioritizing Japanese economic recovery, but insists on presenting the initiative through the Far Eastern Commission to maintain Allied cooperation and congressional support.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles E. Saltzman to William H. Draper, Jr. Regarding SWNCC 384

subfiles.about: Proposes an FEC resolution and policy decision to accelerate Japanese and Far Eastern economic recovery and expand commerce.
subfiles.summary: Major General Frank R. McCoy reviews occupation demilitarization achievements and presents a draft FEC resolution stressing the urgent need for Japanese self-support to relieve American taxpayers. The proposal calls for permitting Allied and Japanese business travel and developing long-range import-export plans that stimulate reconstruction across the Far East.
subfiles.title: Proposed Statement by General McCoy to the Far Eastern Commission on Economic Recovery

subfiles.about: Analyzes State Department redrafting of SWNCC 384 into a formal statement for General McCoy to present to the FEC.
subfiles.summary: Barnett explains that framing economic recovery within FEC policies reassures Allied nations, prevents fears of policy repudiation, and facilitates securing Congressional financial aid.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Robert W. Barnett on Proposed Statement for General McCoy (SWNCC 384)

subfiles.about: Annotated working draft of General McCoy's proposed statement to the Far Eastern Commission on Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Draft text with revisions setting out occupation demilitarization successes, emphasizing the need to relieve U.S. taxpayers, and recommending FEC policies on business travel and trade.
subfiles.title: Annex: Working Draft of Proposed Statement by General McCoy to the Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Records discussion with SCAP Political Adviser Frank Hussey on reparations, foreign exchange rates, the purge, and land reform.
subfiles.from: Department of State Officials (Wisner, Claxton, Rudlin, Moreland)
subfiles.summary: Hussey reviews key occupation concerns, urging quick settlement of reparations and establishment of an exchange rate while asserting the economic purge does not impede recovery.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Conditions in Japan with Frank Hussey

subfiles.about: Commends University of Washington research on Japan's economic structure and provides a list of reference materials.
subfiles.summary: Hunsberger endorses proposed research on Japan's trade and regional complementarity, offering State Department consultation and enclosing a bibliography of declassified documents.
subfiles.title: Letter from Warren S. Hunsberger to Professor Nathanael H. Engle on Japanese Economic Research

subfiles.about: Presents a critical analysis of SANACC 381/2, warning against attempts to bypass the Far Eastern Commission on Japanese recovery.
subfiles.summary: Robert A. Fearey criticizes SANACC 381/2 for circumventing the Far Eastern Commission, arguing that genuine Allied cooperation requires submitting the recovery plan directly to the FEC. He warns that unilateral maneuvers will provoke resistance from China, the Netherlands, and the Philippines. Fearey also critiques specific provisions regarding post-treaty intervention powers, shipping, and tariff adjustments.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Robert A. Fearey to W. Walton Butterworth on SANACC 381/2

subfiles.about: Responds to a congressional inquiry regarding an alleged FEC document on Japanese economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Kirlin advises Representative Donohue that the requested document does not exist and encloses a report on Far Eastern Commission activities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Florence E. Kirlin to Representative Harold D. Donohue

subfiles.about: Proposes compromise procedures between the Army and State Departments for advancing SANACC 384 on economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: Draper proposes submitting State's redraft to the FEC while transmitting the amended Army paper to MacArthur and releasing it publicly.
subfiles.title: Letter from William H. Draper, Jr. to Frank G. Wisner on SANACC 384
